_readme: Transient-wake allow/veto rules for classify.py. Each entry's `note` is provenance -- why this exact string is here -- extracted from the original inline comments when this table still lived in Python. See CONTRIBUTING.md and SECURITY.md before editing: a change here decides which errors get retried automatically, so it needs a human security review, not just a green test run.

TRANSIENT_PATTERNS.note: Connection-closed family, original allowlist. Observed 34 times; genuinely interrupted background a background job.

Same family as mid-response (stream cut, not a refusal). Historical instance: 2026-06-16 one session -- owner manually resumed 28s later ("network hiccuped just now, continue, retry, continue"). No log survives to confirm whether this was actually scanned live at the time; only that this exact wording was missing from the allowlist.
Family-wide safety net added alongside the two entries above, to catch any future third wording beyond "before producing a response".

Stream-interruption family. Owner testing on 2026-07-10 found this exact string missing from the allowlist. Cross-checked against the real log line by line, severity differed per session: one session errored at 19:23 and was not resumed until 02:26 (~7h real stall, with a 19:23:51 log line confirming it was scanned live and misjudged "no transient pattern matched") -- this is the actual gap this addition closed. one session errored at 03:06:33 and was resumed at 03:07:36 (~63s) -- the same misjudgment fired, so the gap was real, but the manual retry beat the next scan cycle by little.

Same stream-interruption family and investigation as "response stalled mid-stream" -- this is the exact wording one session hit. That session and another session both had the same real gap (each logged one matching "not matched" misjudgment), but a user retry / teammate message landed in the same scan window each time, so no extra stall was actually observed -- recorded to prove the gap was real, not to claim either session waited long.

Family-wide safety net: any text containing "mid-response"/"mid-stream" is semantically a physically-cut stream (the model's own wording is typically "the response above may be incomplete"), not a refusal -- classified transient so future wording variants don't slip through the same gap again.

Rate-limit / infra-throttling family, original allowlist. Observed 26 times collectively across this family. This is infra-side throttling, not a usage-quota limit -- see NON_TRANSIENT_VETO for the quota-exhaustion family, which must NOT be treated as transient.

NON_TRANSIENT_VETO.note: User-rejection family, original allowlist. Rule #1: never auto-retry a rejected/denied action.
403 Request not allowed is a permission problem, not a transient one, original allowlist.
Permission family, original allowlist -- same condition as 403, worded differently.
Quota-exhaustion family, original allowlist -- a real usage-quota problem (not infra throttling); retrying does nothing useful and can loop forever.
Auth family, original allowlist -- retrying does nothing, the user has to log back in.

Real request-construction-error family, original allowlist. Golden negative: this exact class of 400 schema error (tool_use_id mismatch, a background job) was manually retried 6x and failed every single time -- automatic retry would just loop forever.
Same 400-schema golden-negative family and investigation as the plain \b400\b rule above.
